title: Minimax Pointwise CATE Estimation under Finite Outcome Moments and Rough Nuisances
banked_reason: Not salvageable within scope — bank downgraded, or re-anchor the proposal (rewind D-1.2).
gap_reasons: The p=2 elbow already appears in [Kennedy et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2203.00837v4), and the nuisance-saturation half-plane is an algebraic consequence rather than an additional independent contribution.
The theorem settles a fixed-point, scalar, known-uniform-design experiment with public exponents, while the software connection supplies no implemented or demonstrated practical improvement.

Its honest intervals establish rate optimality with extremely conservative constants: at the representative tuple, the displayed length certificate becomes smaller than the full target range only around n=10^39.65, constraining the package's practical inference significance.

The published [Liu–Lian neighbor](https://scholars.cityu.edu.hk/en/publications/kernel-based-adaptive-huber-mean-regression-with-heavy-tails-and-/) has accessible publication metadata and an abstract but inaccessible theorem text, so precise priority comparison requires source verification without blocking the field floor.

proof_attempt_summary: The original-record finite-moment point-CATE frontier and maximal positive two-dimensional nuisance-saturation region passed both mathematical and decision panels with no findings; the final cold referee capped the sound package at subfield (7.3 versus field floor 7.4). Independent MAIN validity confirmed no bounded in-scope repair. The earlier 651-node Lean graph is stale relative to the strengthened theorem: F4 did not converge and F5 never ran, so this bank claims no final strengthened-theorem build, source-grep, or axiom certification.
tldr:
For every public \(\kappa=(p,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in(1,2]\times(0,1]^3\), the original-record minimax absolute risk and whole-class \(0.90\)-honest connected-interval expected length for the original mean CATE at \(1/2\) both have order \(\max\{n^{-r_{\mathrm o}},n^{-r_{\mathrm i}}\}\), uniformly for \(n\ge2\), without a logarithmic multiplier. Explicit total estimators and intervals attain this order; exact-uniform original-law comparisons prove the matching converse. The result establishes the tail-dependent interaction exponent below finite variance and the necessary and sufficient boundary for retaining the same-law revealed-nuisance order. At \(p=2,d=1\), agreement with the Kennedy--Balakrishnan--Robins--Wasserman elbow holds on the anchor paper's stated regime \(\gamma\ge\beta\) and is independently reproved here for exact uniform design. When \(\gamma<\beta\), the present theorem independently covers the remaining domain and is automatically in the oracle phase because \(S/\gamma>1\). EconML CausalForestDML is the named consumer for the same original-mean CATE task; the theorem supplies a precision and coverage benchmark and explicit robust alternatives without asserting optimality or coverage for its default forest. The theorem uses no separate control-mean range restriction: the conditional moment envelope supplies the public projection constant \(C_G(p)=3\,10^{2/p}\le300\). The headline displays the named program \(\mathfrak H_\kappa^{\mathrm{explicit}}\), including its exact two-block covariance numerator and denominator, public localization and truncation thresholds, positive-denominator safeguard and clipped public-radius interval. With \(\bar\alpha=\min\{\alpha,(p-1)/2\}\) and \(\bar\kappa=(p,\bar\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\), propensity smoothness above \((p-1)/2\) is saturated: on that slice, \(\mathcal M_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal M_{\bar\kappa}\), the same program attains the oracle order uniformly over the enlarged saturation class, and the established oracle comparison proves matching risk and honest-length lower bounds there. The original class, maximum rate and oracle-survival boundary are unchanged.

The exact two-dimensional positive nuisance-saturation region is
\[
 \mathcal A_\kappa=\left\{(u,v):0<u\le\alpha,\ 0<v\le\beta,
 \left(\frac1\gamma+\frac2{p-1}\right)u
 +\left(\frac1\gamma+\frac1q\right)v\ge1\right\}.
\]
For \((\widetilde\alpha,\widetilde\beta)\in\mathcal A_\kappa\), put
\(\widetilde\kappa=(p,\widetilde\alpha,\widetilde\beta,\gamma)\).
Both H\"older inclusions on \([0,1]\) preserve radius \(20\), so
\(\mathcal M_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal M_{\widetilde\kappa}\).
The phase expression
\(B(u,v)=(u+v)/\gamma+(2u+pv)/(p-1)\) is increasing in both
coordinates. Consequently both risk-rate and length-rate formulas at
\(\kappa\) and \(\widetilde\kappa\) equal \(n^{-r_{\mathrm o}}\).
The named program \(\mathfrak H_{\widetilde\kappa}^{\mathrm{explicit}}\)
evaluates the unchanged formulas with
\(\widetilde a=\min\{\widetilde\alpha,(p-1)/2\}\),
\(\widetilde s=\widetilde a+\widetilde\beta\) and
\(\widetilde d=q-\widetilde a(2-p)/p\).
Direct reuse of the upper calculation supplies its total Borel map,
public tuning, denominator safeguard, finite-sample risk, whole-class
\(0.90\) coverage, samplewise length and small-sample certificates.
The established oracle lower comparison at \(\widetilde\kappa\) gives
matching risk and honest-length orders there; no recursive headline
invocation is used. Equality in the half-plane is included and zero
exponents are excluded. Constants are uniform only on compact subsets
inside this positive admissible region. The previous
\(\alpha_\star=[1-\beta/\gamma-\beta/q]_+/(1/\gamma+2/(p-1))\)
family, with \([z]_+=\max\{z,0\}\), remains exactly the slice
\(\widetilde\beta=\beta\), and the capped-propensity conclusion remains
its universal corollary. Below the half-plane the established interaction
lower bound precludes this oracle order. Decreasing \(\gamma\) also
precludes it, because \(r_{\mathrm o}(w)=wq/(w+q)\) is strictly
increasing for \(w>0\), and the oracle lower comparison holds on every
such enlarged class. Thus this two-dimensional family exhausts positive
coordinatewise H\"older enlargements at fixed \(p\) retaining the
original oracle order. The original target, model, frontier,
oracle-survival boundary and software claim are preserved.
gap: Pointwise CATE theory separates effect smoothness from nuisance regularity, but its bounded-outcome fluctuation proof does not characterize arbitrary conditional finite-\(p\) outcome kernels. The exact-uniform design also requires a converse whose laws retain every transition region. Scalar robust means and generic canonical-kernel bounds do not resolve the coupled smooth-effect, rough-confounding frontier.
fill: The central open question couples observable attainment, original-law necessity and public finite-sample honesty. The supporting results derive the oracle experiment, local covariance bias and feasible heavy projections, and isolate an interaction obstruction. The full frontier remains an output. No tail-shape, clipped-mean regularity, supplied main-experiment propensity or nuisance-fit condition enters the model.
